newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Short Australian debt firm ahead wages result.
newsitem.headline: Short Australian debt firm ahead wages result.

text.p: *Short-dated Australian debt was firm ahead of the Australian Industrial Relation Commission's verdict on the "living wage" claim at 2.00 p.m. (0400 GMT).
Short-dated Australian debt futures were firm ahead of the Australian Industrial Relations Commission's long-awaited verdict on the "living wage" claim.
Expectations centre on a A$12 per week pay award, which would add some 0.5 percent to annual wages growth, keeping it within the Reserve Bank's 4.0 to 4.5 percent comfort zone, analysts said.

"A decision granting much more than A$12-14 could see the market sell off quite sharply. A decision closer to A$8 is likely to spark a fairly positive reaction," said Su-lin Ong, fixed income economist at Hambros Bank.

The expected A$12 per week safety net pay award would be a compromise of the government's A$8 per week proposal and the Australian Council of Trade Unions' A$20 per week safety net and 8.75 percent minimum rate adjustment.
June bill futures were trading at a day's high of 94.07, equating to a cash rate of 5.93 percent and compared with current official interest rates of 6.0 percent.

"The short-end is looking fairly solid in anticipation of the wage result and in front of the CPI tomorrow," one trader said. "We are seeing some buying of long bonds, which would otherwise be drifting."

There is a school of thought that if the wage outcome is moderate and the March quarter CPI on Wednesday is benign it would leave the RBA scope to ease policy to keep the economic recovery in motion given the patchiness of recent data.
The Reserve Bank board meets on May 6, by which time quarterly average weekly ordinary time earnings would have been released on May 1.

Meanwhile, the long-end of the market is being restrained by further weakness in U.S. Treasuries in Tokyo trading after the lower close in New York ahead of this week's two and five year note auctions.
The market's firmer bias saw spreads to the U.S. narrow, erasing much of Monday's widening, and are expected to tighten further if the "living wage" outcome proves moderate.
The yield curve also steepened as the short end outperformed in anticipation of favourable wage and inflation results.
